newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel follows Brent futures upward.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel follows Brent futures upward.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil prices rose tentatively on Thursday, following Brent crude futures higher.
But little physical business was done, with traders sceptical about the strength of crude's technical and short-covering rally.
"There is still a lot of oil out there," said one dealer, wary of the flurry of activity on the paper market.
"This is just a technical adjustment and reality will intervene soon to bring it crashing back down."
High sulphur cargo prices picked up a notional $3 to $82/$84 a tonne cif in Europe but no trades were heard done at that price.

A good quality cargo from a French refinery was heard sold on Wednesday to a trader at 50 percent fixed $78.50 fob and 50 percent fob high quotes plus $3.50 a tonne, which helped prop up numbers. Morning interest in Scandinavian high sulphur cargo disappeared by mid-afternoon with no deal heard done.

Barge prices jumped up to an $87 a tonne high, from $83 on Wednesday, before sinking back gently, as one buyer bid up values to increase profits on a quotes-related cargo deal, traders said. Bids later slipped back to $82.
"We are awaiting clarity, there's a lot of confusion out there about the situation in the market," said one trader.
Low sulphur fuel oil cargo markets stayed dead all day, traders reported, with no demand for the product.
